hook: Gates co-founded Microsoft with Paul Allen in 1975 and ran it as chief executive until 2000, then moved over the following years to full-time work at the foundation he had established in 2000. He left Microsoft's board in 2020 but stayed on as a technology adviser to Satya Nadella. He writes regularly about AI's effects on work, health and education, from his 2023 essay The Age of AI has begun to a 2026 essay calling for firm limits on the technology.

timeline.event: Co-founds Microsoft with Paul Allen on April 4
timeline.impact: Starts the company that becomes a dominant force in personal computing software.

timeline.event: Hands the CEO role to Steve Ballmer and establishes the Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation
timeline.impact: Begins shifting his attention from running Microsoft to philanthropy.

timeline.event: Leaves his day-to-day role at Microsoft in June
timeline.impact: Moves to full-time work at the foundation.

timeline.event: Steps down as Microsoft chairman on February 4
timeline.impact: Becomes a technology adviser to new CEO Satya Nadella.

timeline.event: Named a recipient of the Presidential Medal of Freedom
timeline.impact: Recognised with Melinda French Gates for the foundation's work.

timeline.event: Steps down from Microsoft's board of directors on March 13
timeline.impact: Ends his formal governance role at the company while remaining a technology adviser.

timeline.event: Publishes The Age of AI has begun on GatesNotes on March 21
timeline.impact: Argues that generative AI is as significant as the microprocessor, the PC, the internet and the mobile phone.

timeline.event: Tells The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon in March that AI could shrink the working week to two or three days within about a decade, and in the foundation's 25th year commits to giving away virtually all his wealth over 20 years
timeline.impact: Extends his AI commentary to labour and sets a deadline for his giving.

timeline.event: Publishes the essay The turbulent AI era is here on August 26
timeline.impact: Calls for serious AI regulation, work reserved for humans and a tax on AI to slow the replacement of workers.

quick_facts: Left Harvard in 1975 to co-found Microsoft with Paul Allen.
Was Microsoft's chief executive until 2000 and chairman of its board until February 4, 2014.
Stepped down from Microsoft's board on March 13, 2020, remaining a technology adviser to CEO Satya Nadella.
Is chair and a board member of the Gates Foundation, established with Melinda French Gates in 2000.
Founded Breakthrough Energy, launched in 2015 to back clean energy technology.
Received the Presidential Medal of Freedom in 2016, jointly with Melinda French Gates.

achievements.title: Co-founder, Microsoft
achievements.impact: Co-founded the company in 1975 and led it as CEO for about 25 years, building it into a dominant supplier of personal computer software.

achievements.title: Gates Foundation
achievements.impact: The foundation gave away more than $100 billion in its first 25 years, and Gates has said he intends to give away virtually all of his wealth over the following 20 years.

achievements.title: Breakthrough Energy
achievements.impact: Founded in 2015 to fund entrepreneurs and technologies working on climate change.

achievements.title: Public commentary on AI
achievements.impact: His 2023 essay The Age of AI has begun compared generative AI to the microprocessor and the personal computer, and his 2026 essay The turbulent AI era is here proposed setting aside some work for people and taxing AI to slow job displacement.

achievements.title: Presidential Medal of Freedom
achievements.impact: Named a recipient in November 2016 with Melinda French Gates for their foundation's work on global health, poverty and education.
